tip: The '-abilir' slice adds can or may: 'kullanabilir' = can use, from 'kullan' plus 'abilir'.
To turn an adjective into a yes/no question, add 'mu' after it: 'boş mu' = is it empty.
The '-e' ending marks a destination: 'hastaneye' = to the hospital, from 'hastane' plus 'ye'.
To finish doing something, the action takes '-meyi' before 'bitirdi': 'pişirmeyi bitirdi' = finished cooking.
The '-tan' ending means from: 'mutfaktan' = from the kitchen, from 'mutfak' plus 'tan'.
'var' means there is and sits at the end, with the place in the '-da' form: 'kutuda ... var' = there is in the box.
The from and to pair uses '-ten' then '-e': 'çiçekten çiçeğe' = from flower to flower.
The '-yı' ending marks a specific, definite object: 'baklavayı' = the baklava, a known particular one.
After 'kaç' meaning how many, the noun stays singular: 'kaç fosil', never 'kaç fosiller'.
The '-ken' ending means when or while: 'küçükken' = when I was little.
A proper name takes an apostrophe before any suffix: 'Beyoğlu'nda' = in Beyoğlu.
The '-müş' ending marks hearsay or a fresh realization: 'bugünmüş' = apparently it is today.
The '-arak' ending turns a verb into by doing it: 'koşarak çıktım' = I went out running.
Between X and Y is X 'ile' Y 'arasında', with 'arasında' last: 'park ile okul arasında' = between the park and the school.
The '-il' slice makes a verb passive: 'yıkılacak' = will be demolished, with no doer named.
After a base verb, 'için' means in order to: 'gitmek için' = in order to go.
Ability comes from '-ebilir': 'dene' (try) plus '-ebilir' gives 'deneyebilir', and a 'y' slips in between the two vowels.
A specific object takes '-i': 'dilleri' means those particular languages, not 'diller' for languages in general.
No word for costs or is: 'bilet kırk beş lira' states the price directly. Turkish drops the linking verb here.
'olsun' is the let-it-be form of 'olmak': 'kutlu olsun' literally means may it be blessed, the way you congratulate.
'sonra' (after) takes the '-tan' ending on the noun: 'yolculuk' becomes 'yolculuktan', so 'yolculuktan sonra' means after the trip.
Motion toward a place uses '-e': 'bahçe' becomes 'bahçeye', meaning to the garden.
Location uses '-de': 'ev' plus '-de' gives 'evde', at home. It answers where something happens.
To show whose, the owner takes '-in' and the thing takes '-i': 'öğrencilerin ödevleri' means the students' homework.
'bit-' alone means end by itself; add '-ir' to give it a doer: 'bitirdi' means he finished it, not just it ended.
For a span of time up to now, add '-dir' to the amount: 'iki yıldır' means for two years now.
'-ınca' means when or once: 'emekli ol' plus '-unca' gives 'olunca', once I retire. It sets the timing of the next clause.
'-muş' can mark a realization: 'unutmuşum' means it turns out I forgot, something you notice rather than state flatly.
For will be, Turkish uses 'olacak' ('olmak' plus future '-acak'): 'proje başarılı olacak' means the project will be successful.
Obligation uses '-malı': 'yap' plus '-malı' plus '-yız' gives 'yapmalıyız', meaning we must prepare.
